synopsis: South Africa is the only jurisdiction found to legally require automatic slow-down and braking, effective since 21 December 2022; the remaining regions are characterized as having risk-based duties without an automatic-braking mandate [f164, f2125]. MSHA's surface mobile equipment rule took effect on 19 January 2024 and was enforced from 17 July 2024, requiring written safety programmes and consideration of technology rather than mandatory collision avoidance [f5842, f5843]. The EU Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027, before the prototype arrives; the Digital Omnibus on AI entered into force on 27 July 2026, but its machinery provisions rely on secondary summaries with conflicting Annex I application dates of 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 [f6696, f6698, f10309, f10310]. ISO 21815 standards are not inherently law, and the most concrete mining acceptance numbers come from industry specifications rather than legislation [f2062, f173, f2112]. No universal legal acceptance rule for virtual evidence or published off-road regulator commitment to accept it was found, and the glossary states that simulation cannot replace a prescribed physical test [f11037, f258, f12004]. Planning therefore calls for jurisdiction-specific applicability sign-off, explicit checks on simulation acceptance and assessor engagement, while unresolved issues include the final status of the proposed heavy-vehicle AEB rule, data-governance requirements, and unverified EU Data Act and Cyber Resilience Act application dates [f10165, f10235, f11126, f1333, f5800, f10817].
